lens: cluster (PROTOCOL_V3 Addendum H): losses that come together, and an algorithm that adapts
written: 2026-11-12, after part 1 (anatomy, descriptive) and BEFORE any guard variant was evaluated
reserved: 1 trial, to be declared in a second batch (written here before it runs) only if needed
data: the ten sleeves' own one-position chains re-simulated on in-sample frames only (repro.py: identical to the official files except the two trades still open on 2021-12-31, closed at the last in-sample bar); FP costs (mode fp) and costs x1.5 (mode stress, every trade re-simulated on the widened quotes)
reference: the account: every trade of the ten chains in entry order (same-minute ties: ASCII order of name_sym), one base stake each, not taken if its stop is closer than 3 spreads of its fill bar (none in sample), or if 6 positions are open, or 2 on the same market; a position is open for a new entry until its exit time is strictly before the entry time; no compounding; R = multiples of the base stake
engine: r2/tracks/autopsy/cluster/engine.py run_engine (codes in its docstring). The guard multiplier g is computed first; a trade with g > 0 then needs a free slot (caps 6 / 2). A trade not taken stays in its sleeve's chain (followed on paper). State at an entry time t: results of trades whose exit time is < t only.
window_of_judgement: entries 2018-02-01 .. 2021-12-31 (the engine runs over the whole in-sample history so that its state is warm); days and weeks of the FP server clock (New York + 7 h), booked at the exit time; years by entry year

metrics.E: expectancy per base stake = sum(m R) / sum(m) over the trades taken (for skip rules: the mean R of the trades taken)
metrics.AL: average loss per base stake = -sum(m R | R < 0) / sum(m | R < 0) over the trades taken
metrics.total: sum(m R) at the same base stake (no rescaling)
metrics.also_reported: n taken, sum of stakes, win rate, PF, worst day, worst week, maximum drawdown (cumulative R in exit order), longest run of losing days (days with a booking) and of losing weeks (calendar weeks), every figure by year, per sleeve what is removed, and the same at an equal number of base stakes deployed (total, worst day, worst week, drawdown x sum(m_ref)/sum(m))

candidate_criteria.a: E >= 1.20 x E_ref  (branch 1)  OR  [AL <= 0.80 x AL_ref AND E >= E_ref]  (branch 2)
candidate_criteria.b: total >= total_ref; and if the variant deploys more base stakes than the reference (sum(m) > sum(m_ref)), also total x sum(m_ref)/sum(m) >= total_ref
candidate_criteria.c: the metric of the branch that passed (E for branch 1, AL for branch 2) is better than the reference's in at least 3 of the 4 years 2018-2021
candidate_criteria.d: (a) and (b) also hold on the costs x1.5 run against the costs x1.5 reference
candidate_criteria.e: every declared neighbour improves on the reference too: the metric of the branch better than the reference's AND total >= total_ref (variants declared without neighbours are not eligible)
candidate_criteria.f: causal: truncation test (decisions identical when everything after the decision time is removed: trade outcomes not yet known are masked; and, for every candidate, price frames cut right after the decision bar and all ten sleeves re-simulated)
candidate_criteria.ranking_if_several: highest E / E_ref; tie: highest total. At most one portfolio change is carried forward.
